meta.scope: Suriname batch 4 — Deeper oil/fiscal architecture (Staatsolie contribution, GranMorgu fiscal outlook, financing), social-protection reform, non-mining growth, and residual trade/debt relationships. Extends coverage beyond the initial ~30.

candidates.title: Staatsolie contributions to the State
candidates.description: Taxes, dividends, royalties and related transfers from Staatsolie (and gold participations) to the central government. Material current fiscal contribution pending offshore first oil.
candidates.notes: Operational fiscal link. Recent annual contributions on the order of hundreds of millions of USD (e.g. ~USD 400 m cited for 2025) form a large share of mineral revenues.

candidates.title: GranMorgu / Block 58 fiscal outlook
candidates.description: Projected lifetime fiscal income from the GranMorgu development (independent estimates in the mid-to-high tens of billions of USD). Central medium-term fiscal prospect.
candidates.notes: Transformative fiscal node. Continuously cited as the main source of the expected step-change in GDP and government revenue from ~2028; institutional framework for managing the windfall is still being completed.

candidates.title: Staatsolie financing for Block 58 equity
candidates.description: Bond issuance and syndicated loan used by Staatsolie to fund its 20% participating interest in GranMorgu (order of USD 2 bn combined financing).
candidates.notes: Financing counterpart of the state equity stake. Continuously cited in discussions of contingent public-sector exposure and of the cost of securing a larger share of future oil revenues.

candidates.title: Social protection reform / National Social Protection Strategy
candidates.description: Ongoing reform of the social-assistance system (digitalisation, targeting, registry accuracy, reduction of duplication) under the National Social Protection Strategy.
candidates.notes: Institutional reform node. Continuously cited in IMF and domestic poverty analysis as the main attempt to improve the efficiency and targeting of transfers before the oil windfall arrives.

candidates.title: Non-mining / non-natural-resource GDP
candidates.description: GDP excluding mining and oil extraction. Has shown more robust growth than the mineral sector in recent stabilisation years.
candidates.notes: Analytical counterpart to headline GDP. Continuously cited as evidence of recovery outside the volatile mineral cycle; still small relative to the prospective oil step-change.

candidates.title: District Nickerie — western agricultural
candidates.description: Western coastal district with significant rice and agricultural activity. Secondary economic pole outside the greater Paramaribo area.
candidates.notes: Coastal agricultural node. Completes the set of major districts beyond Paramaribo/Wanica and the deep interior.

candidates.title: Block 52 / PETRONAS exploration
candidates.description: Offshore exploration block with multiple discoveries (including gas). Complements Block 58 as a second major international exploration/development front.
candidates.notes: Secondary offshore node. Continuously cited alongside GranMorgu as evidence of broader basin potential beyond the first development.

candidates.title: Debt restructuring with China and other bilateral creditors
candidates.description: Restructuring agreements with China (ICBC, EXIM and related) and other bilateral/commercial creditors that formed part of the post-crisis debt resolution.
candidates.notes: External-debt architecture node. Continuously cited as a necessary condition for restoring external viability pending oil revenues.

candidates.title: International reserves
candidates.description: Stock of international reserve assets. Rebuilt from crisis lows; adequacy metrics have improved under the stabilisation programme.
candidates.notes: External-buffer node. Continuously cited in exchange-rate and stabilisation analysis; levels remain sensitive to mineral export cycles and project-related import spikes.

candidates.title: Rice production and exports
candidates.description: Rice production and export statistics. Principal traditional agricultural export and rural livelihood activity on the western coast.
candidates.notes: Traditional agro-export node. Continuously cited in non-mining diversification and rural-employment analysis.

proposed_edges.basis: Contributions to the State are the fiscal expression of Staatsolie’s operations and participations.
Fiscal-income projections are derived from the GranMorgu production and cost profile.
The bond and loan package financed Staatsolie’s 20% equity in GranMorgu.
The National Social Protection Strategy is the reform framework for the existing transfer system.
Non-mining GDP is the residual of total GDP after excluding mineral extraction.
Block 52 is the second major offshore exploration front in the same basin.
Chinese and other bilateral restructurings are components of the overall debt resolution.
Changes in reserve assets appear in the balance of payments.
Nickerie is the principal rice-producing district.
